## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Dukanikkhepa* is a section of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī* (Ds 2.3.2), the first treatise of the canonical Pali Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Situated in the third major division of the work alongside the *Tikanikkhepa* (Ds 2.3.1), the text sets forth the analytical exposition and classification of the dyads (*duka*) of the Abhidhamma matrix (*mātikā*) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral lists two modern translations of the text in two languages [SuttaCentral].
SuttaCentral identifies passage-level parallels in the *Dukaatthuddhāra* (Ds 2.4.2) of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, the *Khuddakavatthuvibhaṅga* (Vb 17) of the *Vibhaṅga*, the *Adhiṭṭhānahāravibhaṅga* of the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 17), and multiple sections of the *Mahāniddesa* (Mnd 1, 2, 4, 15) and *Cullaniddesa* (Cnd 5) [SuttaCentral]. Additional resembling parallels are noted with the *Tikanikkhepa* (Ds 2.3.1), other *Niddesa* sections (Mnd 3, 10, 14; Cnd 6, 23), and doctrinal groupings in the *Dīgha Nikāya* (DN 33, DN 34) and *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 9.29, 9.30; AN 10.79, 10.80) [SuttaCentral].
Computational text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus corroborates this shared terminology, detecting 18,612 matching passages across 277 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Both SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus agree on significant overlaps with the *Tikanikkhepa* (Ds 2.3.1), the *Dukaatthuddhāra* (Ds 2.4.2), and the *Khuddakavatthuvibhaṅga* (Vb 17), with further dense reuse found in the *Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅga* (Vb 6), *Dhātukathā* (Dt 2.9, 2.10), and the *Paṭṭhāna* [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus identifies conceptual and lexical matches between the *Dukanikkhepa* and Sanskrit and Tibetan Abhidharma literature, notably Vasubandhu's *Pañcaskandhaprakaraṇa*, Sthiramati's *Pañcaskandhakavibhāṣā*, Ghoṣaka's *Abhidharmāmṛta*, Asaṅga's *Abhidharmasamuccaya*, and the *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
